subject: Late-window circuit-breaker fix — advisory and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.example>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@brightcart.com>, BrightCart Support <support@brightcart.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Late-window circuit-breaker fix — advisory and next steps

Hi Sam / BrightCart team,

Quick note to let you know we applied an emergency fix at 11:30 PDT this morning to address an edge-case in our serving runtime that was causing repeated CPU spikes on the path that handles long-conversation KV cache merges. To avoid broader degradation we activated a runtime circuit-breaker which temporarily returned 503s for a subset of long-lived streaming sessions (estimated impact window: ~11:27–11:34 PDT).

What you should know:
- Scope: ~0.6% of API requests from your production fleet (calls with >4k token context and streaming enabled).
- Visible behavior: short-lived 5–10s failures or aborted streams; successful retries typically recovered within 2–4s.
- Mitigation: we flipped the circuit-breaker and deployed a targeted patch that prevents the KV merge path from spinning under this pattern.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) sharing a compact telemetry dump that isolates BrightCart sessions during the impact window (attached).
2) dev-led follow-up postmortem and permanent fix plan scheduled for Thursday, Jul 30 — we will share a write-up and planned rollout cadence.
3) If you saw any customer-facing incidents you’d like prioritized for credits or escalation, reply with timestamps and affected endpoints and we’ll fast-track.

Sorry for the short notice — we chose the minimal-risk action to avoid cascade impact. If you prefer an engineering sync now, I can pull Dev and Stephanie in for a quick call.

Attachments: telemetry_dump_20260728.json (JSON), circuit_breaker_patch.diff (text)

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0118
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.example>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.example>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>, Sam Torres <s.torres@brightcart.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-window circuit-breaker fix — advisory and next steps

Rachel — quick technical summary to drop into the customer thread:

Root cause (short): an unusual sequence of back-to-back large attention-key merges during KV consolidation led to a scheduling stall in the host-side merge loop. That stall triggered our safety detector which trips the circuit-breaker to avoid GPU starvation.

Why it manifested now: a small increase in BrightCart's long-history chat sessions (higher average context length) in the early morning traffic spike combined with a rare tokenization pattern produced the pathological merge ordering.

Fix applied: patched the merge loop to preemptively yield on large-key merges and added a lightweight heuristics check so the safety detector remains conservative. This is a hotfix; we will schedule a follow-up kernel-level optimization next week.

I attached the patch diff and an excerpt of the telemetry we pulled. Happy to join a call.

— Dev

[Attachment: circuit_breaker_patch.diff (text)]
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@brightcart.com>

Thanks for the heads up, Rachel — appreciate the quick mitigation. A few questions / asks from our ops team:

1) Can you confirm the exact endpoints and request IDs that returned 503s? We’ve correlated a handful of customer tickets to 11:28–11:35 PDT but want a canonical list to attach to our incident reports.
2) Is Redwood going to treat this as an SLA-impacting outage for BrightCart? If so, please provide the formal incident ID and contacts for claims.
3) We’d like to schedule the engineering sync — Thursday sounds good; please put us on the calendar with the expected attendees and an agenda.

Also, we saw one long-running streaming session that dropped mid-prompt — I attached our log snippet (customer-impact-window.csv) so you have our side.

Sam
Sr. SRE, BrightCart

Subject: Re: Late-window circuit-breaker fix — advisory and next steps

Sam — thanks for the details and the log snippet. Quick answers below and plan: 

1) Canonical list: attached is customer-impact-window.csv (from our side) with request IDs, endpoint paths, and timestamps (UTC and PDT). We matched our traces to your snippet and included the corresponding request IDs.
2) Incident ID: RED-INC-2026-0728-01. We will treat this as SLA-impacting and Marcus (cc'd) will own the credit review and paperwork. Please cc finance@brightcart.com when you file the claim and we’ll route it internally.
3) Engineering sync: scheduled Thu Jul 30 at 10:30 PDT. Attendees: Dev (runtime), Stephanie (ops), Marcus (account). Agenda: brief timeline, technical root cause, remediation plan, long-term mitigations, and credit/path-to-closure. Calendar invite sent.

Follow-ups we’re committing to:
- Detailed postmortem doc in Drive (link: https://drive.redwood.example/drive/folders/1A2b3C_postmortem_brief) by EOD Fri Aug 6.
- A safe rollout plan for the kernel optimization next week with staged traffic ramp and monitoring playbook.
- Point-of-contact for expedited SLA claims: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.example>.

Attachments: customer-impact-window.csv

Thanks again for flagging the affected sessions — we’ll have the postmortem and remediation timeline to you shortly.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
